"10.1
That this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to call for the entire records pertaining to the case of petitioner for its kind perusal and thereafter allow the petition.

10.2 That, this Hon'ble Court may kindly further be pleased to direct the respondent No. 2 to decide the case of petitioner for payment of compensation Rs. 14,98,840/- in accordance with the provisions of Section 3-H (sub-section 3) of the National Highways Act, 1956 within stipulated time.

10.3 That, this Hon'ble Court may kindly further be pleased to restrain the respondent No. 2 from paying any compensation to the respondent No. 3 as per the list (Annexure P-5) as published by the authority.

2. Learned counsel for petitioner submits that petitioner is owner of a land bearing khasra No. 229/1 situated at village Mohbhattha, District Bemetara.
The acqusition proceedings were initiated by respondent No. 2 based on the requisition made by respondent No. 1.

However, in the notification issued therein, the Khasra number which was sought to be acquired, is mentioned as Khasra No.
229 only, whereas the khasra No. 229 has been partitioned in two Khasra Nos. 229/1 and 229/3.
At the time of acquisition, the land owned by the petitioner was affacted which is khasra No. 229/1.
However, at the time of passing of award, the compensation was awarded in favour of Kartik who is the owner of the land bearing khasra No. 229/3.
The petitoner, who is an illiterate person after getting the said defect of the khasra numbers in the acquistion proceedings, submitted an application before the Land Acquisition Officer.
However no decision till date has been taken on the same.
Therefore, a direction be issued to the respondent No. 2 to take appropriate decision on the application.

3. Learned counsel for respective respondents No. 1 & 2 however submits that in view of the limited prayer made by the learned counsel for petitioner, they are having no objection but the appropriate remedy available to the petitioner is under Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The petitioner has not submitted any application before the Competent Authority i.e. Collector.

4. At this stage, learned counsel for petitioner submits that in view of the objection raised by the learned counsel for respondents, the petitioner may be permitted to submit a fresh application before the Collector Bemetara for redressal of his grievance.
5. I have heard learned counsel for parties and also perused the documents placed on record.
6. The petitioner has placed on record the copies of the revenue entries in which the name of petitioner is mentioned as owner of the land bearing khasra No. 229/1.

The copy of the award is also placed before this Court and in the award, the khasra number 229/3 is mentioned and accordingly the amount of compensation is awarded.
7.

The grievance of the petitioner is that in the preliminary notification issued for acquisition, only khasra No. 229 was mentioned and at the time of construction of the road, the land bearing khasra No. 229/1 is affected which is owned by the petitioner, but in award compensation is awarded for other khasra number, not affected in construction of road.

8. In the aforementioned facts of the case and also considering the provision under Section 64 of the Act of 2013, I find it appropriate to dispose of the present Writ Petition at this stage permitting the petitioner to submit an application before the Collector under the Act of 2013 as observed above.
In the event, the petitioner submits application under Section 64 of the aforesaid Act of 2013 before the Collector, the same shall be considered and decided in accordance with law expeditiously.
